topic: Database replication and failover; recovery objectives
title: Run a failover drill
instructions:
## Two failures in one afternoon

The four-hour `failover` scenario promotes a database standby at minute 10 and crashes the web server `web-1` at minute 25. The current deployment is one server and a single-zone database. Target: **99.5% availability**.

## Do this

1. Run `failover` as it is and note the availability and what the log says about each failure.
2. Make `orders-db` **Multi-AZ** so failover takes a minute instead of ten.
3. Put `web-1` and a second server `web-2` (in zone **b**) behind a load balancer `web-lb` so a crash drains to the other.
4. Re-run and answer: what were the recovery times before and after?
hints: Edit orders-db and tick Multi-AZ standby.
Create web-2 (medium, zone b), then a load balancer with both as targets. The scenario sends traffic to the load balancer when there is one.
Recovery time: single-AZ failover took 10 minutes; Multi-AZ about 1; the crashed server is drained immediately when the LB has another healthy target.

checks.label: Failover time before
checks.question: How many minutes was the database unavailable in the first run?

realityNote: Recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO) are set per service and tested in drills, because a failover that has never been exercised usually fails in some new way. Synchronous standbys give RPO near zero at the cost of write latency.
